problem: Knowledge graph completion (KGC): predicting missing triples. The paper argues current LLM-based approaches encode graph context as flat text, failing to exploit graph structure, and lists three failures: structural information loss (prompts are long and noisy), static embeddings that do not adapt to query-specific structure, and generic LLM responses driven by pretraining data.
method: DrKGC. (1) Convert incomplete triples into natural-language questions with a template lexicon; (2) train a lightweight model to learn structural embeddings and mine logical rules; (3) use a bottom-up, rule-guided retrieval to extract a query-specific local subgraph; (4) apply a GCN adapter over the retrieved subgraph to produce local structural embeddings, which are integrated into the prompt for LLM fine-tuning. So graph context is used both to construct supervision and inside fine-tuning.
key_assumptions: Logical rules mined from the KG are predictive enough to guide subgraph retrieval.
A compact query-specific subgraph captures the structure needed for the prediction, without long or noisy text prompts.
A GCN adapter over the retrieved subgraph can inject structural information that the LLM cannot infer from text alone.
Restricting the LLM output space to candidates mitigates generic responses.
main_contribution: A dynamic subgraph retrieval-augmented LLM framework for KGC that combines mined logical rules, query-specific subgraph retrieval, and a GCN adapter for structure-aware LLM fine-tuning; claimed state of the art on general KGs and strong performance on domain-specific biomedical KGs with improved interpretability.
datasets: Two general-domain KG completion benchmark datasets (not named in the abstract)
Two biomedical KGs (not named in the abstract)
baselines: Not stated in abstract; related work contrasts KICGPT and KoPA-style generation-based methods
results: Abstract reports superior performance on two general-domain and two biomedical datasets. Full text limitations note fine-tuning is computationally intensive and performance is bounded by the underlying LLM and lightweight model.
limitations: Relies on fine-tuning large language models, which is computationally intensive.
Performance is inherently constrained by the capabilities of the LLM and the lightweight structural model.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: DrKGC retrieves a query-specific subgraph at inference and injects it via a GCN adapter into an LLM prompt for KGC, guided by mined logical rules. The idea instead enriches the *training supervision signal* for KGQA with triples co-occurring in the same source passage, and studies isolated-vs-context regimes plus a repair loop. Same intuition (local context beyond an isolated triple) but different task (completion vs. QA), different context source (rule-guided graph retrieval vs. passage provenance), and different stage (inference+adapter vs. supervision construction).
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.55: both target reasoning that needs more than an isolated triple, but KGC vs. multi-hop KGQA differ. Method overlap 0.6: query-specific subgraph retrieval + LLM fine-tuning with graph context is the closest mechanism found, though not passage co-occurrence. Evaluation overlap 0.25: KGC benchmarks rather than KGQA WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA.
